subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox container exits immediately when no-new-privileges is applied (exec /usr/bin/sleep: operation not permitted)

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit audited way for Docker sandbox users to run without `no-new-privileges` on incompatible hosts, or keep the hardening unconditional and only improve diagnostics?
rationale: The source-level failure is actionable, but the practical recovery paths either weaken the sandbox security boundary or require deciding that affected hosts should remain unsupported except for diagnostics.

options.title: Add explicit dangerous opt-out
options.body: Keep `no-new-privileges` default-on, add a clearly named opt-out with dangerous-config/status reporting, docs, tests, and real Docker proof on an affected or equivalent host.

options.title: Diagnostics only
options.body: Keep the flag unconditional and improve startup/session/status errors so operators can identify the incompatible Docker host and choose a different runtime or version.

options.title: Reject weaker sandbox mode
options.body: Do not add an opt-out or fallback, and close only after maintainers decide this host combination is outside the supported sandbox hardening envelope.

recommendation.title: Add explicit dangerous opt-out
recommendation.body: Keep `no-new-privileges` default-on, add a clearly named opt-out with dangerous-config/status reporting, docs, tests, and real Docker proof on an affected or equivalent host.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a sandbox security/defaults decision, and steipete has the strongest recent history across the sandbox Docker and security-config surfaces.
